Where it began

Irfan Pathan was born in Baroda (Vadodara) on 27 October 1984, and grew up there alongside his elder brother Yusuf, who caught the cricket bug with him. At first, the story goes, his deliveries did not even reach the far end of the pitch. Long training sessions in the heat soon sorted that out, and under the eye of the former India captain Datta Gaekwad he worked his way up through the Baroda age-group sides.

He first played for Baroda's senior side in March 2001. Late in 2003 he lit up a youth one-day tournament in Pakistan, taking 18 wickets at 7.38, including nine for 16 against Bangladesh, and was named player of the tournament. A Test call followed within weeks.

The player

He made his Test debut at Adelaide in December 2003, aged 19, and in Sydney a few weeks later he had Steve Waugh caught behind and bowled Adam Gilchrist. In 2004 the ICC named him its Emerging Player of the Year. Against Bangladesh that December he took 18 wickets in two Tests, and in Zimbabwe in 2005 he took 21 more in two, including his best of seven for 59.

On 29 January 2006 at Karachi he removed Salman Butt, Younis Khan and Mohammad Yousuf in the opening over of the match. Nobody had ever begun a Test with a hat-trick before. In 29 Tests from 2003 to 2008 he took 100 wickets at 32.26, with seven five-wicket innings, and scored 1,105 runs at 31.57.

What made him special

He could swing the ball both ways, which led people to compare him with Wasim Akram. Then the coach Greg Chappell saw a batter in him too. He made 93 as a stand-in opener against Sri Lanka in Delhi, shared a double-century stand with MS Dhoni on his way to 90 in Faisalabad, and late in 2007 reached his only Test hundred, against Pakistan in Bangalore, by hitting Danish Kaneria for six to go from 96 to 102.

The swing came and went over the years, as swing tends to. When it came back, as it did at Perth in 2008, he was man of the match in a 72-run win.

Away from the middle

He was man of the match in the final of the first World Twenty20 in 2007, taking three for 16 as India beat Pakistan, and he was in the side that won the 2013 Champions Trophy. Later he became a commentator and analyst, danced on the reality show Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa in 2015, made his film debut in Cobra in 2022 and captained Bhilwara Kings in the Legends League. His nickname is Guddu.

And finally

He finished his Test career on exactly 100 wickets. Plenty of bowlers spend years chasing a round number. He simply stopped on one.
